chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, who said:

I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) at a funeral for one of his relatives. When he had prayed over the deceased, his guardian said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Return, O Abu Ja'far, having been recompensed, and do not tire yourself because you are too weak to walk.' So I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Permission has been given to you regarding the return, so return, and for me is a need which I want to ask you about.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Rather, it is a merit and a recompense; therefore, he who follows it is recompensed in accordance with the distance he walks with the funeral. As for his permission, we did not come by his permission, nor will we return by his permission.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for following a funeral procession according to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s distinction between social courtesy (*adab*) and spiritual merit (*thawab*), asserting that the reward for following a coffin is intrinsic to the act of accompanying the deceased, regardless of the host's invitation to leave. Scholarly commentary often notes this as a refutation of the view that funeral following is merely a social obligation, emphasizing instead its status as a continuous act of worship and remembrance of death. The Imam’s response underscores the autonomy of divine recompense over human permission in acts of devotion.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Zurara who said,

‘I was with Abu Ja’farasws during a funeral of one of hisasws relatives. So when heasws had Prayed Salaat over the deceased, his guardian said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘Return, O Abu Ja’farasws, having been Recompensed, and do not tire (yourselfasws) because youasws are too weak to walk’. So I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘There is permission for youasws with regards to the returning, so return, and for me is a need which I want to ask youasws about it’. So Abu Ja’farasws said to me: ‘But rather it is a merit and there is a Recompense, therefore he who is able upon walking with the coffin would be Recompensed in accordance with that which he had walked. So, as for his permission, so it was not with his permission that we came over, and it is not with his permission that we would return’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Zurarah who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in a funeral procession of one of his relatives. When he completed the prayer for a deceased, the guardian of the deceased said to abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ’Please return home. May Allah grant you the reward. Please do not become tired.
